text:
emma: Thanks for the AH. Two quick procurement+runway clarifications from product infra: 1) pilot vs commit: if we run a 90-day paid pilot with a vendor and it looks good, is that counted against runway as committed cash? 2) currency / FX concerns for overseas vendors 1% swings are making budgeting tricky.

ben (Infra): Also, if pilot invoices are monthly but vendor wants a PO, can we still use P-card for the first month to move faster?

maria (CFO): Good q's. Short answers: pilots that are month-to-month are Opex and counted as cash outflow when paid; multi-month prepaid pilots are treated as committed cash immediately. PO vs P-card: prefer PO for anything > $5k or recurring monthly billing. P-card ok for one-off tools < $2k.

olivia (FP&A): On runway modeling: we deduct cash when it's contractually obligated or pre-paid. For a 90-day pilot invoiced monthly, runway impact is month-by-month. If pilot is prepaid 90d, it's deducted up front.

emma: That makes sense. Any fast-track for pilots tied to customer demos (need infra in 2-3 days)?

dylan (Finance Ops): We can fast-track up to $10k for customer-facing pilots if manager approves and Finance Ops is cc'd. Submit quick intake: FIN-320 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-320) and tag "pilot-fast-track". We'll aim for same-day review for clear revenue opportunities.

kira (Product): Re: FX: can we ask vendors to invoice in USD? Some vendors only invoice in EUR/GBP. How do you want us to model the risk?

maria (CFO): Preferred: invoice in USD. If vendor invoices in other currencies, include FX buffer in the budget (we currently use a 3% contingency baseline; for volatile currencies, increase to 8-10%). FP&A will run sensitivity if it's > $25k impact.

ben (Infra): Suppose pilot converts into a committed Dedicated pool with a 6mo term and vendor offers a 10% discount for commit. Who signs, and does this need exec review?

maria (CFO): Commitment thresholds unchanged: Procurement + Finance Ops for standard commits; exec sign-off required for annualized >= $50k. For a 6mo commit, compute annualized run-rate (monthly cost * 12). If annualized >= $50k, escalate to execs.

emma: Noted. What about negotiated exit clauses? we should insist on opt-out after 30 days if SLA not met, correct?

dylan (Finance Ops): Yes, always negotiate termination or service credits for infra commitments. Add SLA and exit window to the intake form. Procurement will push for these clauses.

olivia (FP&A): Also please provide two cash scenarios: base-case and downside (20% lower utilization) so we can show runway sensitivity.

procure-bot: Created FIN-320-5: "Pilot fast-track - 90d vendor trial for eval cluster" assigned to dylan.

sam (CEO): High-level: we back experiments that show clear path to cost reduction or revenue. Fast-track is there for customer demos and high-confidence pilots, but loop in Finance early to avoid surprises to runway.

emma: One last thing 1) any change to monthly P-card reconciliation timelines? we've had delays reconciling vendor credits.

maria (CFO): Reconciliation cadence remains EOM plus 5 business days. If you anticipate credits or refunds, flag them in the intake so FP&A can net them in the month of credit.

kira (Product): Action items for teams: 1) use FIN-320 for pilot fast-tracks, 2) ask vendor for USD invoicing if possible, 3) include two utilization scenarios and FX buffer if non-USD, 4) cc Finance Ops + Procurement early.

emma: Thanks everyone, will file FIN-320 and include the demo timeline. Appreciate the quick answers. :pray:
